note: Professionally accomplished — head chef for twelve years, time in several of the world's top-ranked restaurants, and about to open his own place — so 'successful' holds. Everything else fails. Income fails outright: no job, savings being consumed by the restaurant, no credit card, and an unprompted worry about making rent. Health is not the neglected area but an active crisis: a cervical spine injury, a shoulder that will not raise, cortisone, chiropractic care, chronic sciatica, IBS and fourteen ulcers last year, summarised by him as living in pain every second of every day. The ask is rescue, not good-to-great — "it's now or never." And the exclusion criterion catches him on its second clause: he is not fifty pounds overweight, but he is emphatically gym-averse, saying so four separate times, most plainly "I hate the vibe... I just don't vibe with anything in the gym. It's just not my thing." This is the most consequential ICP data point in the batch: the furthest-outside prospect produced the largest single contract value at $7,200, on the most aggressive terms, and no criterion in the stated ICP would have stopped it — least of all a clinical one, which the ICP does not contain.
